title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the page where Grothendieck formulates what is now called the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture. Under the heading 'Questions' he sets up the following.

Setting:
- S is an integral scheme of finite type over Spec Z, dominant over Z, with generic point y.
- X is smooth of finite type over S.
- E is a locally free O_X-module with a flat (integrable, curvature-zero) connection relative to S.

Definition ("niveau zéro" / "intégrable"). The induced connection on E_y over the generic fibre X_y is said to be 'of level zero', or 'integrable', if there is a finite étale surjective cover of X_y on which E_y becomes trivial as a module with connection, i.e. it has a full set of horizontal sections. In modern terms the connection has finite monodromy, equivalently it is algebraically integrable (all solutions algebraic).

Complex-analytic restatement. For an extension K of k(S), in particular K = C, this is equivalent to saying that the representations of the transcendental fundamental groups pi_1 of the connected components of X_C, given by the monodromy of E_C, factor through finite groups.

Marginal note. He wants a definition of the notion that is directly local, presumably on S or on X, in the étale topology.

Generalization to groups. The notion can be varied for an arbitrary group scheme G of finite type over S. One takes a G_X-torsor P on X with a curvature-zero connection relative to S, and the same question can be asked for such torsors.

The page breaks off at 'Remarquons que si la connexion de E est intégrable, on…'. The next page completes it:
- If the connection is integrable, there is a neighbourhood U of y in S such that the p-curvature of E_s vanishes for all s in U of characteristic p > 0.
- Equivalently this can be tested at closed points only.
- 'Question: la réciproque est-elle vraie?' This converse is exactly the p-curvature conjecture.
- He then splits the rank-1 case into two questions: (a) torsion of the class of E in Pic(X_y); (b) a closed 1-form whose reductions mod p are locally logarithmic has an integer multiple that is a dlog, checked mod p via the Cartier operator C(omega) = omega.

The previous page handles the classification of rank-one modules with integrable connection, and of stratifications, when X is proper.
errors: 'composantes connexes de E_K' should read 'composantes connexes de X_K'. This is a slip in either the manuscript or the transcription.

The 'necessary direction' (finite monodromy implies vanishing p-curvature for almost all p) is correct. It follows by spreading the finite étale cover out over an open of S, where the bundle becomes trivial with connection, and p-curvature vanishing descends along étale maps.
No mathematical error is visible. The definition is stated only at the generic point, and the margin itself notes that a local definition is lacking.

ideas.what: Converse question: vanishing of p-curvature for almost all p implies finite monodromy (algebraic solutions). The question itself is on the next page; this page sets up the definitions.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (unpublished, c. 1969–70), publicized by N. Katz (1972, Invent. Math.; 1982, Bull. SMF)
ideas.where_published: Not by Grothendieck himself. Stated and credited to him in Katz, 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations' (1972).

ideas.what: Definition of 'level zero' / integrable connection: it becomes trivial (as a module with connection) after a finite étale cover; equivalently the complex monodromy is finite.
ideas.modern_name: connection with finite monodromy / algebraically integrable connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schwarz, Fuchs); arithmetic formulation by Grothendieck–Katz

ideas.what: Generalization of the question to G-torsors with flat connection, for an arbitrary group scheme G of finite type over S.
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature conjecture for principal G-bundles / G-connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed later in work of Katz (1982, differential Galois group version) and Y. André (2004)

ideas.what: Necessary direction: integrable implies p-curvature zero for almost all p (at closed points of an open set of S).

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks for a definition of 'integrable/level zero' that is directly local, rather than defined only at the generic fibre. This suggests he had in mind a local or étale-local formulation of finite monodromy relative to S.
missed.quote: il faut une déf. de cette notion directement locale sur ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. Relative or local versions of algebraic integrability over arithmetic bases are not standard, but the point is probably known in spirit.

missed.claim: The page shows Grothendieck himself posed the conjecture for torsors under arbitrary finite-type group schemes G over S, not just for vector bundles. This goes slightly beyond what is usually attributed to him via Katz.
missed.quote: Cette notion peut se varier aussi pour n'importe quel schéma en groupe de type fini G sur S, on prend sur X un torseur P sous G_X, avec connexion à courbure nulle rel/S. La question précédente peut se poser aussi pour de tels groupes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical attribution of the G-bundle form of the p-curvature conjecture. It includes non-reductive and non-affine G, such as abelian schemes, where torsors relate to Bost/André-type algebraicity results.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the original formulation of the famous p-curvature conjecture, already credited to Grothendieck via Katz, so the content is known. Two details are mildly new to the record: the 'niveau zéro' terminology, and his explicit extension to torsors under arbitrary group schemes G of finite type.
transcription_corrections: 'S intègre pl géom.' is uncertain. It probably reads something like 'S intègre, plat' (integral and flat); the reading is unclear.
'se ferment à travers des groupes finis' should read 'se factorisent à travers des groupes finis'.
'composantes connexes de E_K' is likely 'composantes connexes de X_K'.
'dans K de k(S)' is probably 'dans [une extension] K de k(S)'.
'au sens (Zar)' is uncertain; it may refer to a sense/reference rather than Zariski.
